title: DietrichGebert/ponytail
claim: Ponytail — a prompt/skill layer that makes coding agents ruthlessly minimal: ship the least code that works (YAGNI as a one-line install for 20+ agents).
why_good: Attacks the #1 complaint about coding agents — overengineered slop — and the pull is real: ~90k★ in six weeks, 62 contributors, an npm package, and it works across Claude Code, Cursor and the rest.
value: The wedge into agent behavior management: teams pay to enforce code-minimalism and style policy across every agent seat (org-wide config, policy packs, reports on bloat avoided).
risk: It's prompts, not software — near-zero moat. Any agent vendor can ship a 'concise mode' toggle, and skill-pack virality decays as fast as it spikes.
pick_reason: The project is too vague and resembles a concept rather than a clear, monetizable product.

zh.claim: Ponytail —— 一层让编码 agent 极简的提示/技能:只写能跑的最少代码(把 YAGNI 做成一行安装,支持 20+ 种 agent)。
zh.why_good: 正面打编码 agent 最大的痛点——过度设计的垃圾代码;而且势头是真的:六周约 9 万星、62 位贡献者、有 npm 包,Claude Code / Cursor / Codex 通吃。
zh.value: 切口是 agent 行为治理:团队为「在每个 agent 席位上统一强制极简与代码规范」付费(组织级配置、策略包、审计)。
zh.risk: 它是提示词不是软件,护城河近乎为零;任何 agent 厂商加个「简洁模式」开关就能覆盖,技能包的病毒式增长退得和涨得一样快。
zh.hook: 开发者受够了 AI 把 40 行能解决的事写成 400 行——愤怒到愿意装一个 9 万星的陌生人提示层，但没人证明过这些层真的有效。
zh.does: 可一键安装进 20+ 编码代理的提示/技能层，强制极简主义——只写能跑的最少代码、显式标注刻意的捷径。npm 打包，自带尺寸/成本/延迟的小型基准。
zh.gap: 所有提示层都在卖感觉，没人卖证据——社区基准显示 ponytail 把任务通过率从 15/15 拉到 10/15，而市面上没有任何产品在你把代码库交给这些层之前先验证它们。
zh.counter: 核心产物就是一段系统提示——零护城河、随手可抄，作者握着 9.1 万星的心智份额；Anthropic/OpenAI 随时能把'精简模式'做成一个开关。
zh.differentiator: 别抄提示——做证明：一个能对任何提示包/技能跑真实代理任务基准并公布通过率差异的平台，就是这些讨论串在呼唤的'消费者报告'。
zh.consumer_angle: 本身没有——这是能力信号：提示层的分发是病毒式的，但'信任'才是没被满足的需求。

hook: Developers sick of AI agents shipping 400 lines where 40 would do — angry enough to install a stranger's prompt layer 91k-stars deep, but nobody has proven any of these layers actually work.
does: A prompt/skill layer installable into 20+ coding agents that forces ruthless minimalism — ship the least code that works, mark deliberate shortcuts. One-line install, npm-packaged, with a small self-run benchmark on size/cost/latency.

voices.quote: I've seen many system prompts that reduce token usage, explain things clearly, and plan better. But I never see them tested against benchmarks, so how can we know they're working?
I have zero incentive to even consider using this when there's a real risk in it degrading model performance. Actual benchmarks would be super appreciated.
I don't want it to mark anything as ponytail. This should be a tool for writing better code, not to leave its branding everywhere.

gap: Every prompt layer sells vibes, none sells proof — a community benchmark in the repo showed ponytail dropping task success from 15/15 to 10/15, and no product exists that verifies these layers before you trust your codebase to them.
counter: The core artifact is a system prompt — zero moat, trivially copied, and the author owns 91k stars of mindshare; agent vendors (Anthropic, OpenAI) can absorb 'concise mode' as a toggle any quarter.
differentiator: Don't copy the prompt — build the proof: a harness that benchmarks any prompt pack/skill against real agent tasks and publishes pass-rate deltas, the 'Consumer Reports' these threads are begging for.
consumer_angle: None in itself — this is a capability signal that prompt-layer distribution is viral but trust is the unmet need.
